clue.text: Old group take in lake in ancient city

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: to take in food is to eat it
L is the map abbreviation for lake
Thebes was a city of ancient Egypt and of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A historian describes a band of old settlers occupying a lakeside spot in some ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the phrase 'take in', a verb for eating; only the second 'in' is the container signal. Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt and also of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles were the famous Liverpool pop band of the 1960s, now long disbanded, hence an old group.

clue.text: Lie in bed tossing? It's most unpalatable

definitions.note: a superlative phrase defining a plain adjective: inedible is the extreme of unpalatable

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters are taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lies awake in bed, restless, perhaps after a dreadful dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing' looks like what the restless sleeper does, but it reorders the eight letters of the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be eaten at all is at the extreme end of being unpleasant to taste.

clue.text: All over the place after street disturbance

indicators.note: 'after' tells you which piece comes second when the two are joined

blocks.note: ST is the usual abbreviation for street
something rife is widespread, found everywhere

explanation.surface: Debris is strewn everywhere following a riot in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All over the place' reads as messy, but here it means widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or trouble, the kind of unrest a public disturbance involves.

clue.text: They won't go off with US men that lack energy

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: dude is American slang for a man
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A complaint about lethargic American men who never leave.
explanation.walkthrough: DUDES loses one E. 'Go off' suggests leaving, but the definition means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Duds are shells or bombs that fail to explode, so they never detonate as intended.

clue.text: Club supports discharge of one throwing weight about

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below the other

blocks.note: a discharge from a gun is a shot
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A sports club backs the sacking of a bully who throws their weight around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing weight about' sounds like bullying, but it literally describes the field athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is an athlete who hurls a heavy metal ball, so literally throws a weight.

clue.text: Rabbi led astray by one unprepared for speech

indicators.note: being led astray means going off course, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also forms part of the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: A rabbi is misled by a speaker who turned up without notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led' does double duty: its letters join the fodder, and with 'astray' it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ad-libs improvises remarks on the spot, having made no preparation for speaking.

clue.text: Mature former pupil promoted wine shop

indicators.note: promotion moves things upward, and in a down entry going up reverses the order

blocks.note: mature and aged both mean grown old
OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: An older alumnus has been given a better job at an off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: AGED followed by OB is read upwards in this down clue. 'Old boy' is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or shop selling wine, and in American usage a corner grocery.

clue.text: Pressure to remove last horse from moorland

indicators.note: removing the final one means a closing letter is dropped

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a heath is open uncultivated moorland

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to take the final pony off the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation H is removed from the end of HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the heat on someone is to apply strong pressure, so heat means coercion or stress.

clue.text: Remain firmly resolved to execute ruffian

blocks.note: to hang someone is to execute them
a tough is a thug or ruffian

explanation.surface: A judge stays determined to put a thug to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffian' is a noun here, so its synonym is the noun 'tough', not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Hang tough is an American idiom meaning stay determined and refuse to give in under pressure.

clue.text: Doctor (single) is a bit of a bore

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
single and one both mean a lone unit

explanation.surface: An unmarried doctor turns out to be rather tedious company.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'single' look like a marital status, but it is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a monotonous humming sound or a person who talks tediously, either way something boring.

clue.text: Good lives on, the opposite for criminals

indicators.note: taking the opposite swaps each word for its antonym

blocks.note: the opposite of good is bad
the opposite of living on is dying

explanation.surface: Goodness survives, but villains meet the reverse fate.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words before the comma are flipped to their opposites, and the two results are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Baddies is an informal word for villains or wrongdoers, the people on the wrong side of the law.

clue.text: Travel wearing explosive weapon

indicators.note: what is worn wraps around the wearer, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle
TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive

explanation.surface: Someone journeys strapped into a bomb vest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive weapon' looks like one phrase for a bomb, but 'weapon' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, and also the name of Britain's submarine-launched nuclear missile system.

clue.text: Go slowly, as risk-taker drops margins

indicators.note: the margins are the edges, so dropping them removes the outer letters

blocks.note: a gambler takes risks

explanation.surface: A cautious move as a punter cuts their stake margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Margins' sounds like betting odds, but it just means the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed and leisurely pace, a stroll rather than a hurry.

clue.text: Sketch growing part of what's up for approval

definitions.text: growing part of what's up for approval

blocks.note: first meaning: a small rough drawing

blocks.clueFragment: growing part of what's up for approval
blocks.note: second meaning: the thing that grows on the digit raised to show approval

explanation.surface: A rough draft of a proposal is being expanded before it goes up for a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's up for approval' is the raised thumb of a thumbs-up, and its nail keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a small quick sketch, and literally the nail on the digit raised in a thumbs-up gesture.

clue.text: It was commonly read during troubled times

definitions.text: It was commonly read during troubled times

blocks.clueFragment: It was commonly read during troubled times
blocks.note: surface reading: a popular book or newspaper people turned to in hard times
setter's reading: a law formally proclaimed aloud to disperse crowds during civil disorder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly read' suggests popular reading matter, but it was literally read out by magistrates to unruly mobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1714 British statute had to be proclaimed to a rioting crowd before force could lawfully disperse it.

clue.text: Less substantial artist with true representation of books etc

indicators.note: a representation renders something in a new form, so the letters are recast

blocks.note: lite food is a reduced, lighter version
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slighter painter offers a faithful depiction of books and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: LITE is the marketing spelling of light, as in low-calorie food. RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the general term for written works such as books, poems and plays.

clue.text: It can locate position with match — true or false?

definitions.note: a question standing for the noun phrase: a test of whether something is true or false

blocks.note: in golf the lie is where the ball rests, its position
a detector is a device that finds things
a test match is an international cricket match, and a test is a contest

explanation.surface: A quiz question about some gadget that pinpoints locations and pairs them up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one riddle, but it splits into parts: 'It can locate position' reads as a finder of positions, so the position word comes first. A test is a cricket match between countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph examination measures a subject's physiological responses to judge whether their statements are honest.

clue.text: Examine outskirts of city, one looking quite attractive

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: to eye something is to look it over
only the edge letters of the word are used
the comma has to be read as 'and', which sits between the edge letters

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the suburbs and spots a good-looking person.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is short of letters as printed: the comma must stand for 'and', placed between the outer letters of 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for someone or something visually appealing but perhaps lacking substance.

clue.text: Trouble following older cast to wealthy location

indicators.note: coming after something places this piece second in the join
a casting reshapes metal in a mould, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An ageing film cast causes bother on location at some rich resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors, but it signals a reshuffle of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary South American city of gold, now any place of fabulous riches.

clue.text: Smile more excitedly as one delivers drinks

indicators.note: excited things jump about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters are taken as written

explanation.surface: A waiter grins broadly while handing out the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene fits a waiter, but the nine letters before 'excitedly' rearrange into the specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the restaurant's wine waiter, who recommends and serves the bottles to diners.

clue.text: Poor medium I left without difficulty

indicators.note: something that has left has gone away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
to do something without difficulty is to do it easily
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disappointing psychic says they walked out effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a psychic, but it is the clothing size M; then the letter I departs from EASILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means meagre or contemptibly small, as in a measly portion, so of poor quality or amount.

clue.text: House Democrat in heavy defeat setback

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
a setback sends things backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat

explanation.surface: A political report of a Democrat losing badly in the House of Representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like the US chamber, but it means a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal dynasty that ruled England from 1485 to 1603, a house in the family sense.

clue.text: Notified in hearing when being charged

definitions.note: past participle: charged a fee for passage

indicators.note: what is heard is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: to be notified is to be informed

explanation.surface: A defendant is informed in court as they face criminal charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' and 'charged' suggest a courtroom, but they signal sound and a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To toll a road or bridge is to levy a fee on users, so something tolled has been charged for.

clue.text: Pretend to have arrangement that accommodates song

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room, so one piece houses the other

blocks.note: a pact is an agreement or arrangement
a lay is an old word for a ballad or song

explanation.surface: Someone fakes a deal with a recording studio to fit a song in.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY is a poetic word for a song, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To play-act is to behave theatrically or insincerely, putting on a show to make believe.

clue.text: Letters sent going after job

blocks.note: first meaning: mail
second meaning: a position of employment

explanation.surface: Job applications are mailed out to chase a vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is also a third hint, as in the prefix of postwar.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is British for mail, and also a position or appointment someone holds at work.

clue.text: Youngster hanging around stores getting tips off little spoiled child

indicators.note: taking the tips off removes the front ends of the words that follow

blocks.note: small and little are synonyms
a brat is a spoilt, badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A teenager loitering in shops is warned off a spoilt little kid.
explanation.walkthrough: Both SMALL and BRAT lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mall rat is slang for a teenager who spends idle hours loitering in shopping centres.

clue.text: Some opportune moment to hold up consumer choices

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only a portion of the words that follow
holding up lifts things, and in a down entry lifting reads the letters upwards

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A good time to delay giving shoppers their options.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes on offer, the range of options from which a diner picks.

clue.text: Some of loan is deferred when starting firm

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: the initial letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A new business delays repaying part of its loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' looks like a hidden-word signal, but its letters are part of the acrostic.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid and firm are synonyms for something hard, stable and not yielding to pressure.

clue.text: Tory offer could be a runner

blocks.note: Con is short for a Conservative
to tender is to offer formally

explanation.surface: A Conservative's proposal might win the race.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, abbreviated CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a competitor with a real chance, someone who might be running in a race.
